Title: Singapore construction waste resurfaces at closed Pontian dumping site
Article:
PONTIAN: Suspected construction waste from Singapore has resurfaced at a previously closed dumping site in Rimba Terjun here, with 10 lorries linked to various companies detected during an enforcement operation.
Johor Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said 8 of the lorries had records showing they entered Malaysia carrying stone waste, involving four companies.
"Checks conducted with the Customs Department's Import Division at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) found that eight vehicles had entry records showing they had brought in loads of stone waste, involving four companies.
"The remaining two lorries had no corresponding Customs entry records, while checks also found an excavator and heaps of mixed waste at the site," he said.
Zainal, who led the enforcement operation at Lot 3700, Mukim Rimba Terjun, on Nov 13, said it followed public complaints about suspected illegal waste dumping.
He said ownership details of all 10 vehicles had been referred to the Road Transport Department for verification, while the landowner was being identified with the assistance of the Pontian Land Office.
An investigation paper will be opened under Section 71(1) of the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007 (Act 672), which prohibits the unauthorised handling and disposal of controlled solid waste.
Those convicted face a fine of between RM10,000 and RM100,000, imprisonment of between six months and five years, or both.
Johor Local Government and Housing Committee chairman Datuk Jafni Md Shukor is scheduled to visit the site tomorrow at 4pm to assess the situation and review the latest developments.
The discovery has renewed concerns over the illegal dumping of construction waste believed to have originated from Singapore, despite
previous enforcement action
and assurances from Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) that no permits had been issued for construction waste exports to Malaysia.
The issue first came to light in August following reports that large quantities of construction and demolition waste
had been transported into Pontian
and dumped at several locations, including Kampung Sungai Karang, Kampung Sungai Senai and Kampung Simpang Kiri.
Investigations identified nine Malaysian companies allegedly linked to the transportation and dumping activities, prompting the Johor government to establish a special task force involving SWCorp, local authorities, police and the district administration.
On Aug 17, NEA informed SWCorp that Singapore would halt the export of construction and demolition waste to Malaysia. It reiterated that such waste was not permitted to be exported for disposal and reminded licensed waste management facilities to comply with regulations.
SWCorp said all construction waste must be disposed of at approved or gazetted facilities and warned that enforcement would be intensified to prevent further illegal dumping, in line with the Johor Clean City 2030 aspiration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flash floods, fallen trees disrupt traffic in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A heavy late-afternoon downpour caused flash floods along several major roads and uprooted trees at multiple locations in Tanjung Bungah and Paya Terubong today.
State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said emergency response teams were deployed to clear fallen trees and manage traffic flow.
"Our maintenance teams and local authorities are on the ground clearing the debris to ensure road safety and restore smooth traffic as quickly as possible," he said when contacted.
He said fallen trees were reported at several locations, including Lorong Lembah Permai 3, where a tree struck a parked vehicle, as well as near the Chinese Swimming Club, Jalan Bunga Pudak, Jalan Low Yat, Jalan Sri Tanjung Pinang and inside the Cove condominium compound.
He said a traffic light malfunction was also reported at the junction leading to the Tanjung Bungah market, further slowing evening rush-hour traffic.
In Paya Terubong, a fallen tree blocked the road, forcing its closure.
Heavy rain and strong winds were also reported in Kepala Batas.
Motorists are advised to exercise caution and plan alternative routes while clean-up and repair works continue.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rare earths: Radzi warns against repeating colonial-era tin history
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must not repeat its colonial-era experience with tin mining in developing its rare earth industry, Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) has warned.
He questioned the extent of the Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry's (Mosti) involvement in research and development (R&D) into rare earth processing.
"To this day, our country has rare earth supplies but no means, no approach and no technology to process them," he said while debating the ministry's allocation under the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat committee stage.
Radzi said growing interest from world powers in Malaysia's rare earth deposits was evident, noting that 80 per cent of the deposits were located in Terengganu, Kelantan, Perak, Kedah and Pahang, within forest reserves.
"Yesterday, the French president came to Malaysia, and one of his main aims was to discuss the supply of REE, or rare earths, from Malaysia," he said.
He also cited Malaysia's Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the United States, saying rare earths were among its main components.
Radzi highlighted the government's decision to allow the export of up to 100 metric tonnes of raw rare earths for R&D, subject to a commitment to establish processing facilities in Malaysia within three years.
He questioned the extent of Mosti's involvement in developing domestic processing capabilities and whether it was collaborating with local universities.
He said he did not want private companies, particularly those with predominantly foreign shareholders, to reap most of the benefits from the country's mineral resources.
Drawing parallels with the tin industry, Radzi said Malaya produced about 55 per cent of the world's tin in 1900.
"The colonialists plundered the tin. They took the benefits of tin mining back to their own countries. Some of us benefited, but what did they leave behind? All that is left to us is the mining pools.
"In the end, what is left in our country, as the Bachok MP mentioned just now, is badly affected catchment areas, badly affected water supplies and very limited benefit to Malaysia," he said.

Title: Lac Med secures RM21.2mil contract for angiography systems at three hospitals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lac Med Bhd has secured a RM21.2 million contract to supply and integrate advanced angiography systems for cardiology and interventional radiology across three public hospitals in Malaysia.
The contract was awarded to its subsidiary, Lac Medical Supplies Sdn Bhd, by a local healthcare project partner.
The project involves the deployment and integration of advanced angiography systems at University Malaya Medical Centre, Hospital Melaka and Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun in Ipoh.
The latest contract follows another healthcare technology contract announced on Monday, bringing the group's order book to a record high of more than RM300 million.
Chief executive officer Liew Yoon Poh said surpassing RM300 million in its order book marked an important milestone for Lac Med and reflected the continued confidence healthcare providers had in the company's capabilities.
"These consecutive contract wins demonstrate the breadth of our integrated MedTech solutions across both public and private healthcare sectors.
"We remain focused on disciplined execution, strengthening our long-term customer relationships and building sustainable growth through a combination of project delivery and lifecycle services," Liew said in a statement.
The project is scheduled for handover by the fourth quarter of 2028.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prosper Trading secures 56.45pct stake in United Malacca, takeover offer unconditional
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prosper Trading Sdn Bhd, together with its co-founders Tee Kim Tee @ Tee Ching Tee and Tee Cheng Hua, has acquired a collective 118.41 million shares, representing a 56.45 per cent stake in United Malacca Bhd, making its takeover offer for the plantation company unconditional.
In a statement, UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd, on behalf of the offerors, said the acceptance condition was met today after the offerers' aggregate shareholding in United Malacca exceeded the required 50 per cent threshold.
"Pursuant to subparagraph 12.01(3)(b) of the rules, the offeror and joint ultimate offerors shall keep the offer open for acceptances for at least 14 days from the unconditional date, which in any event, shall not be later than the 60th day from the posting date.
"Accordingly, we wish to inform that the closing time and date for the acceptance of the offer have been extended from 5 pm on Nov 23, 2026 to 5 pm on Dec 3, 2026, which is at least 14 days from the unconditional date.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Guan Chong's Q3 net profit surges more than sixfold to RM277.65mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Guan Chong Bhd's net profit surged more than sixfold to RM277.65 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM41.24 million a year earlier, driven by effective management of raw material purchases and cocoa ingredient sales positions.
The group said lower borrowings during the quarter also helped reduce finance costs.
Revenue, meanwhile, fell 38 per cent to RM2.31 billion from RM3.73 billion a year earlier, due to lower selling prices for cocoa products in line with declining cocoa bean prices.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, Guan Chong's net profit rose to RM654.25 million from RM184.04 million a year earlier, while revenue declined to RM6.73 billion from RM11.92 billion.
The group said chocolate demand was expected to improve over the next six months, supported by moderating cocoa prices and continued demand for premium chocolate.
"The premiumisation trend is expected to continue, while the longer-term demand outlook remains supported by growing preference for real chocolate products over compound alternatives.
"However, the potential impact of El Niño weather event in key cocoa-producing regions, together with structural supply challenges and geopolitical uncertainties, could continue to impact market sentiment and supply availability," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
While global cocoa supply has improved from the severe deficits seen previously, the company noted that market conditions remained susceptible to weather-related production disruptions.
Looking ahead, the group said it remained committed to its core cocoa ingredient processing business while expanding into the industrial chocolate segment and optimising production in line with changing market conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Form Three student found dead at Kuala Kangsar boarding school
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR: A Form Three student at a fully residential school here was found dead on the school grounds today.
Several police vehicles were seen entering the school compound this evening, believed to be in connection with investigations into the incident.
However, police have yet to issue an official statement or provide details surrounding the incident.
The student's body is believed to have been taken to Taiping Hospital for a post-mortem.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Policeman killed in motorcycle collision with car in Kota Baru
Article:
KOTA BARU: A policeman was killed after the motorcycle he was riding collided with a car at Pulau Melaka here today.
Corporal Muhamad Alimi Kamarudin, 35, died at the scene in the 5.15pm collision after sustaining serious head and body injuries.
He was attached to the weapons division at the Kota Baru district police station.
Kota Baru district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri confirmed the incident, saying police would issue a statement soon.
Meanwhile, the victim's sister, Siti Nuradila Kamarudin, said the family was informed of the accident at about 5.30pm.
"His wife, Khalidah Adilah Zainuddin, told me she had called him about an hour before the accident.
"He told her he was on his way home to Ketereh after completing his duties," she said.
The 38-year-old personal tutor was speaking when met at the Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia (HUSM) forensic unit tonight.
Alimi, the third of five siblings, was the eldest son in the family. He leaves behind his wife and two children, aged four and seven.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hong Leong Industries posts higher net profit of RM163.67mil in Q1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Industries Bhd posted a higher net profit of RM163.67 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 2027) compared with RM154.90 million in the same period last year.
Revenue rose to RM997.18 million in 1Q 2027 from RM983.38 million previously, primarily attributed to a better sales mix of motorcycle models and lower raw material costs resulting from favourable foreign exchange movements.
Hong Leong Industries declared an interim single-tier dividend of 35 sen per share for the quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, to be paid on Dec 16, 2026.
On the outlook, the company said demand for motorcycles is expected to remain stable amid a more competitive market with the influx of Chinese motorcycles.
"The group will continue to strengthen its product offerings and brand positioning, optimise its product mix, enhance after-sales service, and maintain disciplined cost management," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man killed after tree crushes motorcycle in Selayang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man died when a tree fell and crushed the motorcycle he was riding at Jalan Set 2/8, Setia Eco Templer, Selayang, this afternoon.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 2.19pm.
He said six personnel and two fire engines from the Selayang Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
"Upon arrival at 2.28pm, the operations commander reported that a tree had fallen and crushed an Isuzu lorry and a Yamaha NMAX motorcycle.
"A male motorcyclist was trapped and unconscious. Firefighters then proceeded to extricate the victim," he said in a statement.
Ashrul Riezal said the victim was pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from the Health Ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: LTAT: Size not sole criterion in Boustead Plantations takeover bids
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The bidding process for the takeover of Boustead Plantations Bhd is not based solely on the size of the bidder but also takes into account other criteria, the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) said.
These include the bidder's incorporation status, ability to complete the transaction, strategic suitability and long-term commitment to stakeholders.
LTAT, which controls Boustead Plantations, said its key investment activities were carried out through a competitive bidding process guided by pre-established evaluation criteria, with an emphasis on integrity and good governance.
The fund said bidders must be either government-linked companies (GLCs) or Bumiputera-owned companies, or both, with their status verified by an independent third-party adviser.
"Certainty of execution encompasses proven financing capabilities, while strategic suitability is assessed based on each bidder's capabilities and commitments, rather than solely on the size of the bidder.
"Continuity of existing commitments to the Armed Forces community is also taken into consideration," it said in a statement.
It was reported on Tuesday that LTAT had chosen Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd to take over Boustead Plantations at an estimated price of RM4.3 billion.
Sources told Berita Harian that Achi Jaya was understood to have beaten SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd, two companies with larger plantation operations, in the bidding process.
On the reported proposed transaction, LTAT confirmed that all bidders were either GLCs or Bumiputera-owned companies, or both, in accordance with the guidelines of the Companies Commission of Malaysia.
"The transaction and the evaluation of the bids submitted have been carried out through a stringent process to safeguard LTAT's governance standards and credibility, taking into account the established criteria.
"As the transaction remains subject to ongoing processes and no definitive agreement has been signed, LTAT will make the appropriate announcements and disclosures at the appropriate time, in accordance with the relevant requirements," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JS Solar secures RM30mil rooftop solar, battery storage contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: JS Solar Holding Bhd's unit JS Solar Sdn Bhd has secured a RM30 million contract from NUR Power Ventures Sdn Bhd for a rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (Bess) project.
Under the contract, JS Solar will undertake the engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning works for the project, which is targeted to begin commercial operations by July 1, 2027.
JS Solar Holding said the contract marked further progress in its collaboration with NUR Power Sdn Bhd, the holding company of NUR Power Ventures.
The two companies signed a memorandum of understanding in February to explore strategic collaboration in rooftop solar renewable energy projects.
JS Solar Holding managing director Johnson Chai Jeun Sian said the latest contract would strengthen the company's capabilities in integrated renewable energy solutions.
"The integration of rooftop solar PV and BESS reflects the evolving requirements of renewable energy projects, and this award provides JS Solar with another opportunity to further build our capabilities across both technologies," he said.
"With a targeted commercial operation date of 1 July 2027, our immediate priority will be to ensure disciplined project execution and work closely with NUR Power towards the successful delivery of the project.
"We remain focused on pursuing suitable opportunities that leverage our experience in solar PV while progressively expanding our capabilities in complementary energy solutions such as Bess," he added.
JS Solar Holding said the project would further expand its involvement in Bess, complementing its existing solar PV engineering, contracting and operations and maintenance services.
The ACE Market-listed company provides solar PV solutions for residential, commercial, industrial and utility-scale projects, including rooftop, ground-mounted and floating installations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4 policemen injured in Tapah van crash discharged from hospital
Article:
IPOH: Four of the 10 policemen injured in an accident involving a police van at Km352 of the North-South Expressway (southbound), near Tapah, yesterday, have been discharged from Tapah Hospital today.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin, in a statement to Bernama today, said the remaining six injured personnel were still receiving treatment at three hospitals, with all reported to be in stable condition.
He said four of them were being treated at Slim River Hospital, while the other two were undergoing treatment at Tapah Hospital and Teluk Intan Hospital.
The accident occurred at about 11.35am yesterday when the Maxus van, driven by a policeman and carrying 10 passengers, was travelling from the Perak police headquarters to Melaka.
Alwi said preliminary investigations indicated that the van's rear-left tyre had suddenly burst, causing the vehicle to lose control before crashing into the steel median barrier.
The
accident
claimed the life of a policeman attached to the Batu Gajah district police headquarters, Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Alif Yaacob, 26.
The 10 other policemen in the van sustained injuries, with four suffering serious injuries and six sustaining minor injuries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK cyber safety agency urges firms to limit vulnerabilities after Java warning
Article:
LONDON: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre on Wednesday urged organisations to keep systems updated and reduce exposure to cyberattacks after US and South Korean authorities warned of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used Java programming language.
"We would urge organisations to continue to follow vendor best practice advice and keep their systems up-to-date, as part of the ongoing patch wave," NCSC Chief Technology Officer Ollie Whitehouse said.
He added that AI-assisted vulnerability research and exploit development was reshaping the cyber threat landscape by making it faster and easier to uncover software weaknesses, and said "all organisations should be actively assessing and minimising their external attack surface during this unprecedented time." — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC ends cooperation with Bachar Kiwan after obtaining Kuwait records
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has ended its cooperation with businessman Bachar Kiwan after obtaining official documents and verified records from Kuwaiti authorities for investigations into the recovery of assets linked to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).
The commission said the documents were obtained through a Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) request to Kuwait, making information provided by Kiwan no longer essential to its investigations.
In a statement today, MACC said it had also conducted an internal investigation into several allegations made by Kiwan, as reported by Sarawak Report since Aug 16.
It said the investigation was initiated on the instructions of its chief commissioner to examine the allegations comprehensively and determine appropriate action.
MACC clarified that meetings between its officers and Kiwan were part of normal investigative procedures to examine and verify information provided in connection with efforts to recover 1MDB-linked assets.
"Every discussion was also attended by representatives from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC), and these meetings did not mean that MACC recognised any claims or status asserted by him," it said.
The commission also clarified that Kiwan was not classified as a protected whistleblower under the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010, adding that this had been communicated to him during a meeting on Dec 2 last year.
On allegations concerning rewards and the distribution of proceeds from recovered assets, MACC said the terms cited in the reports were merely draft proposals submitted by Kiwan.
"The proposed terms were never agreed upon or signed by MACC," it said.
The commission also denied involvement in the appointment of lawyers, saying the matter fell outside its jurisdiction.
It said the appointment of legal representatives was entirely at the individual's discretion, while the law firm's withdrawal was its own decision.
MACC said it decided to discontinue cooperation with Kiwan after securing official documents and authenticated records through the MLA process with Kuwait.
"As a result, the information offered by him was no longer a primary requirement for the investigation," it said.
Meanwhile, MACC confirmed that it had recorded a statement from businessman Albert Tei, who visited its headquarters in Putrajaya today to lodge a complaint over the matter.
The commission said it remained open to receiving complaints from any party concerning the allegations, including those lodged with other enforcement agencies such as the police.
It also pledged full cooperation with investigations conducted by other enforcement agencies to ensure the allegations were examined transparently and in accordance with the law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Citaglobal unit to acquire remaining 45pct stake in Germany's Lawi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd's unit Citaglobal Environment Management Sdn Bhd is acquiring the remaining 45 per cent stake in German waste-to-energy (WTE) technology firm Lawi Engineering GmbH for about RM4.32 million.
The acquisition, together with a separate share subscription, will give Citaglobal Environment full ownership of Lawi and its proprietary WTE technology, strengthening its position in waste management and renewable energy.
Citaglobal Environment has entered into a share purchase and transfer agreement with Lawi's remaining shareholder, Dieter Langer, to acquire 26,000 shares representing the 45 per cent stake.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Citaglobal said the RM4.32 million purchase consideration comprises a cash payment of €70,000 (RM318,199) and up to RM4 million to be settled through the issuance of 500,000 new Citaglobal Environment shares at RM8 each.
The share component is structured as an earn-out payment, with the shares to be released to Langer if Lawi achieves an aggregate pre-tax profit of €3 million (RM13.64 million) over the financial years ending Dec 31, 2027, 2028 and 2029.
Separately, Citaglobal Environment will subscribe for 150,000 new Lawi shares at €1 each, totalling €150,000 (RM681,855).
The proceeds will be used mainly to repay shareholder loans and accrued interest owed to Langer, with the balance allocated to Lawi's working capital.
Citaglobal Environment has also agreed to provide shareholder advances of €450,000 (RM2.05 million) to fund working capital for Lawi's recently secured Siam Power project.
Upon completion, Lawi will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Citaglobal Environment.
The issuance of the consideration shares will dilute Citaglobal's stake in Citaglobal Environment from 56.14 per cent to 49.23 per cent, making it an associate rather than a subsidiary of Citaglobal.
As a result, Citaglobal Environment and its subsidiaries will no longer be consolidated in Citaglobal's financial statements. Instead, Citaglobal will recognise its 49.23 per cent share of Citaglobal Environment's results through equity accounting.
Citaglobal said the transactions would give Citaglobal Environment full control of Lawi's proprietary WTE technology, intellectual property and track record of more than 50 power plant projects across 10 countries.
Lawi specialises in designing, installing and commissioning boiler islands and engineering power block cycles for WTE plants using various fuel sources, including refuse-derived fuel, municipal solid waste, industrial waste and biomass.
As of Nov 6, Lawi had an order book of €7.34 million (RM33.37 million) and a project pipeline worth €180.39 million (RM820 million), covering Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam and Indonesia.
The company recorded a net loss of €671,484 (RM3.05 million) and net liabilities of €1.28 million (RM5.82 million) for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025.
Citaglobal said the acquisition would allow Citaglobal Environment to capture Lawi's future earnings, streamline decision-making and deploy its technology across existing and prospective WTE and bio-compressed natural gas projects without relying on third-party technology licences.
The transactions are expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026, while the consideration shares are expected to be issued to a trustee by the first quarter of 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar highlights Malaysia's resilient Q3 growth, 'centrality' policy to woo investors in Shenzhen
Article:
SHENZHEN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim addressed business leaders from Malaysia and China emphasising Malaysia's robust economic trajectory and a pragmatic foreign policy as key pillars for foreign investment.
Speaking at the Malaysia-China High Level Trade and Investment Dialogue organised by the Malaysia-China Business Council, Anwar said the country's strong bilateral ties with the East Asian giant was also a key draw for investors.
The prime minister underscored the Malaysia's positive economic momentum by crediting it to stable governance and thriving international partnerships.
"The central bank just announced today at (noon) that our growth is still maintained at 5.5 per cent for the third quarter, which means that we can reach up to 5.6 and hopefully, you know, we should be about the highest among emerging economies, from a much higher threshold," he said.
Anwar tied this economic resilience to Malaysia's proactive international engagement, with China playing an important role in both trade and investments.
The prime minister was speaking alongside Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz as well as key officials from Mida,
Touching on his engagements surrounding the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting and discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Anwar stressed that political goodwill must translate into tangible business collaboration.
"And with China, as you know, we have established excellent bilateral relations, we have enhanced the level of collaboration through a strategic partnership, comprehensive.
"So how you cement it or make it work is through collaboration not only in terms of political leaders, but economic and business leaders,: he said.
A central theme of the dialogue was Malaysia's foreign policy of neutrality or "centrality", which Anwar framed as a distinct competitive advantage for investors seeking a stable regional base.
He recounted recent high-level meetings with global leaders from the United States, France and Russia, demonstrating Malaysia's open-door diplomatic approach.
"So you can imagine, when we have this policy of centrality, making friends with everybody, this is good for business," he said.
He said this diplomatic stability translates directly to economic security for foreign enterprises.
"It is a precondition for business investments when we have stability, political stability, clear policies, and we have good incentives to attract business," he added.
Anwar also assured investors that his administration remains deeply committed to fighting corruption and ensuring that economic gains ultimately benefit the broader population.
Outlining his economic philosophy, he said: "You have to propel economic growth and use that with good governance, stop waste and corruption, and use the resources to help (the people)."
Anwar concluded his remarks by reaffirming Malaysia's position as a reliable partner to foreign investors, assuring attendees that his economic ministers and agencies stand ready to facilitate business expansion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: State secretary unaware of Ismail's resignation as MB
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said neither he nor his office had received any information about a resignation letter submitted by Datuk Ismail Lasim as menteri besar.
He said Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, had not informed him of any intention to step down.
"I have not received any information about Ismail intending to resign as Negri Sembilan menteri besar. I have also not seen any letter which was said to have been sent to the palace.
"I only learnt about the resignation through social media on the night of Nov 16.
"I have not met him over the past day or two either," he told reporters after attending the launch of the Aulad Sejahtera 2026 Module at Klana Resort.
The event was officiated by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Zafir said he had no further information about Ismail's position, including the outcome of his meeting with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap yesterday.
He said there was no specific standard operating procedure governing a menteri besar's resignation, as such a situation had never occurred in the state.
"However, matters relating to the appointment or assumption of the menteri besar office are provided for under Undang-Undang Tubuh Negri Sembilan 1959," he said.
He added that his office and other state government departments were continuing to operate as usual.
Yesterday, it was reported that Ismail arrived at Istana Hinggap at 5pm, believed to be for an audience with Tuanku Muhriz.
The Yang di-Pertuan Besar's vehicle was later seen leaving the palace through its main entrance at about 6.30pm.
So far, neither the palace nor Ismail has issued a statement on the outcome of the meeting.
Earlier, the Negri Sembilan Palace said a menteri besar's resignation would only take effect after receiving Tuanku Muhriz's consent, in accordance with the Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan.
The palace also said the authenticity of the resignation letter linked to Ismail had
yet to be verified.
Two days ago, Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zamry Abd Kadir was reported as saying that BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received
a copy of the resignation letter,
which was allegedly sent to Tuanku Muhriz.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MGB's Q3 net profit inches up amid weaker construction revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MGB Bhd's net profit edged up to RM12.4 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM12.3 million a year earlier, despite lower revenue.
Revenue fell 30.6 per cent to RM157.7 million from RM227.2 million, mainly due to lower contributions from local construction and property development activities.
MGB said the decline followed the completion of several projects, while new projects were still in the early stages of execution.
This was partially offset by higher contributions from overseas construction projects.
No dividend was declared for the quarter.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, MGB's net profit rose 10 per cent to RM39.9 million from RM36.13 million a year earlier.
Revenue declined to RM569.5 million from RM671.3 million in the same period.
In its construction and trading segment, local revenue fell to RM477.65 million from RM576.73 million a year earlier.
Despite the lower revenue, the segment's pre-tax profit increased by RM17.24 million, mainly due to cost optimisation.
Overseas construction and trading revenue rose to RM77.63 million from RM15.65 million, while its pre-tax loss narrowed by RM6.64 million.
Meanwhile, property development revenue declined to RM200.38 million from RM300.98 million, while pre-tax profit fell to RM23.75 million from RM40.81 million.
MGB attributed the weaker performance to several projects having been completed or nearing completion, resulting in minimal progress.
Group executive chairman Tan Sri Lim Hock San said the group remained focused on cost management and productivity improvements despite the impact of project cycles on third-quarter sales.
"The group remained focused on disciplined cost management and productivity improvement. These efforts enabled the group to maintain its profitability during the quarter," he said in a statement.
Lim said the group continued to strengthen its domestic construction order book through in-house projects and tenders for external contracts.
He added that its operations and industrialised building system precast manufacturing facilities in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, remained unaffected by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
As at Sept 30, 2026, the group's construction order book stood at RM1.62 billion, providing earnings visibility and supporting future growth.
In its property development segment, MGB launched Starlight Residences in late September, marking its maiden development venture in Cameron Highlands.
The project comprises 270 serviced apartments and two retail units, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM129.9 million.
Lim said the group planned to launch new property developments with an estimated GDV of about RM800 million in 2027.
"These launches are expected to benefit from the government's continued efforts to promote homeownership under the 2027 Budget, particularly through stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers and enhanced housing financing initiatives.
"Together with unbilled sales of RM249.6 million as at Sept 30, these launches are expected to support revenue over the coming years," he added.

Title: No major cyber threats affecting Malaysians detected so far, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: No significant cyber threats affecting the people's data or the country's digital infrastructure have been detected so far, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said claims of Malaysians' data being leaked on several dark web sites had yet to be verified, while the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) had not reported any such incidents.
"Sometimes, the data involved may be old data from previous incidents. So far, no such incidents have been reported by Nacsa," he told reporters after a forum session at the Malaysia Idea Conference (SIM), held in conjunction with the 2026 Putrajaya Festival of Ideas (FOI), here today.
Commenting on the government's proactive measures to monitor and address global cyber threats, Fahmi said that Malaysia was accelerating its transition to quantum-safe telecommunications systems and infrastructure.
He said quantum-safe communication technology uses quantum encryption to enhance the security of data transmission and make it more difficult for malicious parties to carry out cyber intrusions.
In this regard, Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and Nacsa had also been instructed to hold discussions with telecommunications companies and fibre-optic network operators to ensure that the country's communication channels remained secure against quantum-based threats.
On cyber threats arising from developments in artificial intelligence (AI), he said that the misuse of AI agents to launch coordinated cyberattacks was among the major concerns globally, although no such threats had been detected in Malaysia so far.
"Certainly, in Malaysia, Nacsa, as the agency responsible, will monitor the situation. Should the threat draw closer or begin to endanger the cybersecurity of agencies and the country's digital infrastructure, we will take action to ensure their security," he said.
Globally, the cybersecurity landscape is facing a rise in AI-based threats, particularly the misuse of autonomous AI agent frameworks, capable of carrying out coordinated cyberattacks without continuous human supervision.
A recent report by Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), earlier this month, revealed that hackers were using AI-based penetration-testing tools, such as Artex, to automate intrusions targeting the financial, government, energy, healthcare and telecommunications sectors.
Meanwhile, a wave of cyberattacks in October and November this year reportedly targeted cooling systems and cold chains at about 700 supermarkets in at least nine European countries, disrupting food supplies and causing losses amounting to tens of millions of euros.
Last Saturday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that Malaysia faced thousands of cyberattack attempts every month, underscoring the need for security teams to be more responsive and better equipped.
On Nov 4, Nacsa raised the National Cybersecurity Threat Level from low to moderate, in response to the prevailing security developments, to ensure that the country's essential services remained protected against possible disruptions.

Title: Pecca's Q1 net profit falls 28.4pct on weaker automotive orders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pecca Group Bhd's net profit dropped 28.4 per cent to RM11.01 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM15.39 million a year earlier, on lower revenue.
Revenue fell 14 per cent to RM52.14 million from RM60.6 million in the same period due to softer order volumes in the group's automotive segment, reflecting a shift in consumer demand ahead of upcoming new model launches.
"Nevertheless, the Indonesia and aviation segments continued to record growth, reflecting steady traction in the group's expansion initiatives," the company said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
The group said it remained focused on enhancing operational efficiency, strengthening cost discipline and expanding its revenue base to support long-term sustainability.
Looking ahead, Pecca said the Malaysian automotive industry recorded a total industry volume (TIV) of 602,633 units for the first nine months of 2026, up four per cent from 579,336 units in the corresponding period last year.
Automotive demand is expected to remain healthy for the rest of 2026, supported by year-end promotions.
"While TIV remained robust, growth has been concentrated in certain brands with new model launches and competitively priced offerings.
"Moving forward, the market is expected to remain competitive, as brands focus on gaining market share. The group observes the market moving through a transition, with consumers increasingly favouring value-for-money offerings," it said.
Despite the competitive operating environment in the domestic original equipment manufacturer segment, the group remained focused on delivering sustainable performance for the financial year ending June 30, 2027.
"Pecca will continue to focus on cost management and production efficiency, driven by improvements in automation and technology, to preserve its cost competitiveness.
"The group will also continue to expand its revenue base by growing its aviation, locomotive and replacement equipment manufacturer export businesses alongside its automotive operations."

Title: Imelda, Modi and Jollibee: Lighter side of Trump's Manila trip
Article:
MANILA: US President Donald Trump was only in Manila for 21 hours on his whirlwind Asia trip, but that was long enough for an awkward encounter with a world leader and some local fast food.
Here are three offbeat moments from the visit:
- The Modi shuffle -
A planned photo shoot with Trump and fellow leaders from Quad security alliance nations turned awkward for at least one of its participants on Wednesday when the US president turned it into an impromptu press conference.
A seemingly annoyed Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi can be seen looking side to side, then lifting his right arm in what appeared to be a signal that it was time to depart.
"Shall we move?" Modi asks.
But the US leader continued responding to a question on the safety of travel for the Thanksgiving holiday after a series of tech outages.
Modi eventually appeared resigned to his fate as he waited for Trump.
The US leader later jokingly attempted to engage Modi by declaring him a "very tough man." It did not elicit a smile.
- 'Long time' friends -
A rumoured meeting between Trump and the now 97-year-old Imelda Marcos materialised Wednesday in the form of a brief tete-a-tete with the family matriarch as he exited a meeting with her son, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
The night before, Trump had lavished praise on the president's parents while noting his "good genetics" at a gala dinner for heads of state in town for an Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit.
"I... don't want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well, and they were great," he said of former dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr and wife Imelda, who fled the country after he was toppled from power in 1986.
In a video shared on X by a White House staffer, Imelda, wearing a red gown and seated in a wheelchair, is seen greeting Trump with outstretched arms, offering him a small gift and dubbing him a "world peace leader."
Trump can be heard saying "I've known her a long time", which a widely circulated Getty Images photo confirms.
The snap shows him seated next to Imelda while attending a party in 1991 with former wife Marla Maples.
- Late-night Jollibee -
Trump's well-known love of fast food was fed before he left Manila on Wednesday, with his Philippine counterpart sharing he'd arranged a late-night delivery of the country's premier takeaway grub: Jollibee.
"I thought a taste of Manila might be good. So last night, I asked my staff to have some Jollibee delivered as a late-night snack for you and your delegation," the Philippine president said.
The snack, Marcos noted, would provide "extra energy" on an Asian diplomatic jaunt that was far from over.
While it was not immediately clear if Trump had actually noshed on the fried delight known as "Chickenjoy" — or the decidedly Filipino sweet spaghetti typically served on the side — at least one other leader definitely did.
On Sunday, the chain posted a snap of Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese happily holding up a fried leg, then chowing down with a bucket of chicken in front of him, part of an event announcing 35 new stores Down Under over the next five years. — AFPs

Title: Appeals Court raises teacher's jail term to 10 years for child sex offence
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today increased an Arabic language teacher's jail sentence from six to 10 years and ordered him to be caned twice for sexually assaulting an eight-year-old female pupil seven years ago.
A three-member panel chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, together with Datuk Ahmad Shahrir Mohd Salleh and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly, unanimously allowed the prosecution's cross-appeal to enhance the sentence imposed on Ahnaf Afiq Shairul Bazri, 35.
"We set aside the sentence imposed by the High Court and substitute it with eight years' imprisonment for the offence under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, and a further two years' imprisonment under Section 16(1) of the same Act, together with two strokes of the rotan.
"The court also orders the respondent to undergo counselling and police supervision for two years upon completion of his prison sentence," said Justice Mohamed Zaini.
The panel dismissed Ahnaf Afiq's appeal against his conviction and sentence imposed by the Muar High Court on March 11, 2026.
It further ordered that a warrant of committal be issued immediately for him to begin serving his sentence, while the bail money is to be refunded to his surety.
In a brief judgment, Justice Mohamed Zaini said the court was not satisfied with the sentence imposed by the High Court, taking into account the gravity of the offences committed by the accused.
"The victim was only eight years old, and the accused had abused his position and the trust placed in him as a teacher entrusted with the care and education of pupils. These were significant aggravating factors.
"The accused also admitted to taking the victim into the room and closing the door. In the circumstances, we find that the conviction is safe and dismiss the appeal against conviction," he said.
He said the victim, who testified as the second prosecution witness (SP2), had given clear and detailed evidence, which was further supported by her prompt disclosure to her mother (SP1) on the day of the incident.
"We do not consider the discrepancy concerning SP2's position when SP4, the victim's schoolmate, entered the room to be sufficiently material to undermine the credibility of her testimony," he said.
On March 19, 2025, the Muar Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Ahnaf Afiq of the charges at the close of the defence case.
However, the Muar High Court subsequently allowed the prosecution's appeal, set aside the acquittal, convicted the accused and imposed a sentence of four years' imprisonment and two strokes of the rotan for the offence under Section 14(a).
The Court further imposed an additional sentence of two years' imprisonment and two strokes of the rotan for the offence under Section 16(1), to take effect consecutively upon completion of the sentence imposed under Section 14(a).
Ahnaf Afiq was charged with sexually assaulting an eight-year-old girl in the workroom of the library at a primary school in Muar, between 10.20am and 11.20am on Oct 3, 2019.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohamed Aznin Mohamed Ariff appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by lawyers Mohd Radzi Yatiman and Nor Hafizah Abdullah.

Title: Ringgit ends lower against greenback, major currencies amid hawkish US rate outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the greenback and other major and regional currencies on Wednesday, amid a hawkish US interest rate outlook.
At 6pm, the local currency fell to 4.1130/1180 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0915/0960.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said traders were still assessing the implications of monetary policy developments for 2026, with their immediate focus on the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for Dec 8-9.
"I suppose traders are still digesting what it means for monetary policy in 2026, and for now the immediate attention is on December's FOMC," he told Bernama.
He said Malaysia's latest third-quarter (3Q) 2026 gross domestic product growth came in higher than the advance estimate, bringing growth for the first nine months of the year to 5.6 per cent, compared with 4.8 per cent in the corresponding period last year.
"Against such a backdrop, we see scope for the overnight policy rate's (OPR) upward adjustment by 25 basis points to be visible in early 2027. However, a deceleration in private consumption growth to 4.3 per cent could put a hurdle to such a decision," he added.
Bank Negara Malaysia today announced Malaysia's economy grew by 5.5 per cent in Q3 2026 against 5.3 per cent in the same quarter of 2025, driven by continued household spending, higher investment activity and stronger exports.  The central bank said export growth strengthened further, driven by technology-related exports across both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products.
At the close, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.
It fell against the Japanese yen to 2.5826/5859 from 2.5736/5766 at Tuesday's close, went down vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.4172/4238 from 5.3991/4051 and edged down against the euro to 4.5144/5199 from 4.5007/5056.
The ringgit also traded lower against its Asean peers.
It depreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.1896/1937 from 3.1759/1796, slipped against the Thai baht to 12.1138/1339 from 12.1014/1201, and declined vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 225.6/225.9 from 224.1/224.4. It lost against the Philippine peso to 6.45/6.47 from 6.42/6.43.

Title: Black panther "Mek Seri" rescued after struggling to walk in Maran
Article:
MARAN: An adult black panther was rescued after it was found struggling to walk at an oil palm plantation in Sri Jaya on Nov 16.
The four-year-old female, named Mek Seri, was rescued by the Peninsular Malaysia Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) and sent to the National Wildlife Rescue Centre (NWRC) in Sungkai, Perak, for further examination.
Pahang Perhilitan director Yusoff Shariff said the department received information from the plantation management around noon about the animal's condition.
He said six Perhilitan personnel, accompanied by a veterinary officer, were deployed to the plantation to assess the panther.
"The panther, named Mek Seri, was captured and initial examinations found it to be in good physical condition, with no serious injuries or broken bones. However, it was having difficulty walking normally.
"As no physical injuries were detected, the 18kg animal was sent to the NWRC in Sungkai, Perak, for further examination by the veterinary team," he said when contacted today.
The black panther, locally known as a harimau kumbang, is a totally protected species in Peninsular Malaysia. Habitat loss and poaching are among the major threats to its survival.

Title: Willownex secures RM28.8mil worth of contracts in Singapore
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Willownex Bhd, formerly known as Willowglen MSC Bhd, has secured three contracts worth a combined RM28.8 million in Singapore for security and surveillance systems.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the non-renewable contracts were awarded to its wholly-owned subsidiary Willowglen Services Pte Ltd on Nov 17.
The largest contract, worth RM11.97 million, was awarded by Woh Hup Engineering Pte Ltd for the supply, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance of a security system.
The contract commenced on Nov 17 and is scheduled for completion on Feb 29, 2028.
The second contract, worth RM10.45 million, was awarded by SP PowerAssets Ltd for the installation and maintenance of door contact systems and closed-circuit television cameras with video analytics capabilities.
SP PowerAssets also awarded Willowglen Services a RM6.38 million contract for the comprehensive maintenance of an integrated security and operations surveillance system.
Both contracts commenced on Nov 17 and are scheduled for completion on Nov 16, 2029.
Willownex said the contracts were expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings and net assets per share for the financial years ending Dec 31, 2027, to 2029.

Title: Ahmad Maslan apologises to Anwar over 'kencing' remark in pantun
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan has apologised to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over his choice of words in a pantun recited during a Dewan Rakyat session on Monday.
In a letter dated Nov 17 and received by the Prime Minister's Office today, Ahmad acknowledged that the wording was inappropriate for a government member.
"I enjoy incorporating pantun into my speeches. The pantun was not included in my winding-up speech and was delivered while responding to two members of parliament's questions on toll reductions and abolitions.
"However, I take full responsibility for those words and the use of 'kencing' in the pantun, which I have withdrawn in parliament," he wrote.
Ahmad said he had no intention of undermining or disrupting ties within the unity government led by Anwar.
"My support for the government and Datuk Seri (Anwar)'s  leadership remains steadfast until the end of the current administration's term.
"As a member of the government, I will continue to carry out my duties professionally, while being mindful of my language and maintaining cooperation when representing the government," he said.
During Monday's winding-up session, Ahmad said the abolition of tolls was a Pakatan Harapan promise, while Barisan Nasional had never made such a pledge.
He then recited a pantun urging the public to support BN and Perikatan Nasional to avoid being
"kena kencing",
a Malay expression meaning to be cheated.

Title: Inari Amertron's Q1 net profit rises 18.5pct to RM61mil on higher revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Inari Amertron Bhd's net profit rose 18.5 per cent to RM61 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM51.5 million a year earlier, supported by higher revenue.
Revenue increased 13.1 per cent to RM368.5 million from RM325.8 million in the same period, mainly driven by higher loading volumes across all business segments.
Inari declared a dividend of 1.00 sen per share, payable on Jan 8.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the semiconductor manufacturer said it remained positive about its prospects for the remainder of financial year 2027.
This was supported by the continued development of its expanded product pipeline, particularly in photonics and advanced packaging, alongside its existing radio frequency business.
It remained mindful of prevailing macroeconomic conditions and geopolitical developments beyond its control.
"The group will continue to advance its manufacturing capabilities, drive operational efficiencies and explore strategic partnership opportunities to strengthen its market position and competitiveness, while remaining focused on sustainable long-term growth," it said.
